title: Genomic DNA Extraction and Genotyping PCR on Mouse Tissues
author: Jayshen Arudkumar
materials: The New England Biolabs (NEB) website can be consulted for the finer details of reaction volumes and components when amplifying using a standard NEB Taq DNA Polymerase and the 10X Standard Taq Reaction Buffer. The primers we used are listed in Supplementary Figure S2. Note that the annealing temperature is subject to variability according to the primer pair sequence. We recommend using 50-100 ng of genomic DNA as the template, as well as assembling all reaction components on ice prior to transferring to the preheated thermocycler. After the PCR, confirm the expected band sizes by carefully visualising the amplified products on a 1% agarose gel.

steps.title: Lyse tissue with buffer
steps.instruction: Add 200 μL Roche Tissue Lysis Buffer (pH 7.4) to a 1.5 mL tube containing the mouse tissue (chop tissue for higher yield). Add 40 μL Roche Proteinase K (~413 μg/μL). Vortex to mix. Incubate at 55 °C for 3 hours (longer incubations optional).

steps.title: Pre‑warm Elution Buffer
steps.instruction: Incubate the required volume of Roche Elution Buffer in a 1.5 mL or 10 mL tube at 75 °C until ready for use, then vortex briefly.

steps.title: Add Binding Buffer and Isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 200 μL Roche Binding Buffer (pH 4.4, contains Tris‑HCl, guanidinium chloride, urea, Triton‑X‑100) to the lysed sample, then add 100 μL isopropanol. Vortex to mix.

steps.title: Centrifuge lysate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 13,000 RCF for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Bind DNA to silica filter
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant into a Roche High Pure Filter Tube placed in a collection tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 RCF for 1 minute. Discard the flow‑through and place the filter tube in a new collection tube.

substeps.instruction: Transfer filter tube to new collection tube

steps.title: Inhibitor removal wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 μL Roche Inhibitor Removal Buffer to the filter tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 RCF for 1 minute. Discard the flow‑through and place the filter tube in a new collection tube.

substeps.instruction: Place filter tube in new collection tube

steps.title: First washing buffer wash
steps.instruction: Add 500 μL Roche Washing Buffer to the filter tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 RCF for 1 minute. Discard the flow‑through and keep the filter tube in the same collection tube.

steps.title: Second washing buffer wash
steps.instruction: Add another 500 μL Roche Washing Buffer to the filter tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 RCF for 1 minute. Discard the flow‑through and keep the filter tube in the same collection tube (ethanol removes remaining salts).

steps.title: Remove residual ethanol
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filter tube at 8,000 RCF for 1 minute. Discard the flow‑through, keep the filter tube in the same collection tube. Then centrifuge at maximum speed for 10 seconds to dry the column and remove any residual ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at max speed for 10 seconds

steps.title: Transfer filter to clean tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the filter tube to a fresh 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Elute DNA with buffer
steps.instruction: Add 200 μL pre‑warmed (55 °C) Roche Elution Buffer (pH 8.5 Tris‑HCl) to the filter tube. Centrifuge at 8,000 RCF for 1 minute to collect the eluate.

substeps.instruction: Add 200 μL pre‑warmed Elution Buffer (55 °C, pH 8.5)

steps.title: Quantify DNA concentration (optional)
steps.instruction: Measure DNA concentration (ng/µL) using a Nanodrop spectrophotometer.
